title: SNOLAB to celebrate Sudbury Neutrino Observatory with Decades of Discovery
excerpt: Celebration Non. 18-19 to include IMAX screening of Messengers, as well as symposium and banquet
content:
Celebration Non. 18-19 to include IMAX screening of Messengers, as well as symposium and banquet

SNOLAB will bring the scientific community together this month to celebrate two significant milestones in the history of the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory.

In December 2015, Dr. Art McDonald shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory’s groundbreaking discovery of neutrino oscillations, which demonstrated that neutrinos have mass. The 10th anniversary of that historic achievement was marked in 2025.
November 2026 marks 20 years since the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory completed its final data run on Nov. 28, 2006, concluding eight years of solar neutrino observations. While that milestone marked the end of the observatory’s operations, it also opened a new chapter as the experiment helped lay the foundation for SNOLAB and a new era of world-leading underground science in Canada.

To commemorate those anniversaries, SNOLAB will welcome Sudbury Neutrino Observatory contributors back to Sudbury for Decades of Discovery, a two-day celebration to honour the experiment’s scientific legacy and the discoveries it continues to inspire.

Decades of Discovery begins on Nov. 18 with an IMAX screening of Messengers, which takes audiences deep inside three remarkable neutrino observatories, including SNO+, SNO’s successor experiment, and IceCube. The 45-minute film is particularly timely following the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded to Francis Halzen for his contributions to IceCube and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from beyond the solar system.

Celebrations will continue on Nov. 19 with a symposium whose speakers will explore the origin, construction, operation and legacy of the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory, followed by an evening banquet.

“The Sudbury Neutrino Observatory changed our understanding of the universe and put Sudbury at the centre of a remarkable scientific story,” SNOLAB executive director Jodi Cooley said in a media release. “Years later, that legacy lives on at SNOLAB through the people, ideas and discoveries shaping the next generation of underground science.”

Full event details can be found on the Decades of Discovery event page right here.

Decades of Discovery — Celebrating the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory

Science North, Special Events Hall

– Messengers IMAX Screening: Nov. 18, 5:30 p.m. to 8 p.m. (Screening at 7 p.m.)

– Symposium: Nov. 19, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

– Banquet: Nov. 19, 5:30 p.m. to 9 p.m. (Banquet begins at 6:30 p.m.)

Nobel Laureate Dr. Art McDonald will join members of the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory collaboration in Sudbury to mark 20 years since SNO completed its final data run and celebrate the experiment’s extraordinary scientific legacy.
